## Overview

Package tela is the public API of Tela, a desktop UI framework written in pure Go: no cgo, no webview, a React-like component model and Tailwind CSS styling.

A UI is a tree of [`Node`](#type-node) values built by function components. Elements (Div, Button, Text...) live in the companion package h, designed to be dot-imported; this package holds the application ([`App`](#type-app), [`Main`](#func-main), [`Run`](#func-run)), hooks and component boundaries ([`UseState`](#func-usestate), [`C`](#func-c), [`CP`](#func-cp)...), events ([`MouseEvent`](#type-mouseevent), [`PointerEvent`](#type-pointerevent), [`DragEvent`](#type-dragevent), [`KeyboardEvent`](#type-keyboardevent) with the [`Key`](#type-key) and [`Code`](#type-code) constants, [`FocusEvent`](#type-focusevent), and the [`ChangeEvent`](#type-changeevent), [`InputEvent`](#type-inputevent), [`CompositionEvent`](#type-compositionevent), [`SelectEvent`](#type-selectevent) and [`SubmitEvent`](#type-submitevent) of text fields and forms), [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref), the typed style props for h.Style, colors, and the [`Previews`](#type-previews) that `tela snapshot` and `tela inspect` render.

```go
import (
    "github.com/kuronosu/tela"
    . "github.com/kuronosu/tela/h"
)

func Counter() tela.Node {
    count, setCount := tela.UseState(0)
    return Div(Class("flex flex-col items-center gap-6 p-10"),
        H1(Class("text-5xl font-bold"), Textf("Count: %d", count)),
        Button(Class("px-6 py-3 rounded-xl bg-indigo-500 text-white"),
            OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setCount.Set(count + 1) }),
            Text("Increment")),
    )
}

func main() {
    tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Demo", Width: 800, Height: 600, Root: Counter})
}
```

[`Main`](#func-main) runs the app and, if no window can be opened, prints the error and exits with status 1; [`Run`](#func-run) returns the error instead.

### Styling

Static styling uses Tailwind v4 classes (h.Class). A class that depends on state goes in h.If, which takes props as well as nodes, and dynamic values go through typed props, which apply after the classes:

```go
Div(Class("rounded-xl p-4"), If(selected, Class("ring-2 ring-indigo-500")),
    Style(tela.Width(w), tela.Bg(tela.Hex("#1e1e2e"))))
```

Values that change every frame (a drag position, a progress bar) can be deferred to a later phase with [`TranslateFn`](#func-translatefn), [`OpacityFn`](#func-opacityfn), [`WidthFn`](#func-widthfn) and [`HeightFn`](#func-heightfn): a [`UseValue`](#func-usevalue) read inside them redoes only that element's layout or paint when it changes. Colors are extended sRGB; see [`Color`](#type-color).

### Components

A component is a function returning a [`Node`](#type-node). Wrapped in [`C`](#func-c) (no props) or [`CP`](#func-cp) (comparable props), it becomes a component boundary: an element with its own hook state, rebuilt on its own when that state changes. [`CP`](#func-cp) skips the build when its props are == to the previous ones and nothing it reads changed (automatic skipping, as in Jetpack Compose); [`Memo`](#func-memo) does the same with a comparison function.

```go
Div(tela.C(Header), tela.CP(Card, CardProps{Title: "Inbox"}))
```

Calling a component function directly runs it inside the caller, whose hook slots its hooks would take: in dev mode a hook called from a function that is neither the component being built (or a function literal inside it) nor a custom hook panics with the fix. A custom hook is a function named UseXxx or useXxx that calls hooks for the component that calls it; a struct of [`Value`](#type-value) pointers is a good thing for one to return, since it is stable and comparable:

```go
type Drag struct{ X, Y *tela.Value[float32] }

func UseDrag() Drag {
    return Drag{X: tela.UseValue(float32(0)), Y: tela.UseValue(float32(0))}
}
```

A plain function without hooks (a wrapper that styles its children) needs no boundary; h.Fragment(children...) passes the children it receives through.

### Hooks

Hooks keep state and run code across builds, with React's names and semantics:

- [`UseState`](#func-usestate) (and [`UseStateSet`](#func-usestateset), [`UseStateUpdate`](#func-usestateupdate)) and [`UseReducer`](#func-usereducer) hold state; their [`Setter`](#type-setter) and [`Dispatcher`](#type-dispatcher) are comparable, stable and safe from any goroutine.
- [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect) runs code after the frame is presented and [`UseLayoutEffect`](#func-uselayouteffect) after layout, with cleanups, when their dependencies change; [`UseMount`](#func-usemount) runs once, on mount (with its cleanup on unmount), [`UseEffectDo`](#func-useeffectdo) has no cleanup and [`UseUpdateEffect`](#func-useupdateeffect) skips the first build.
- [`UseInterval`](#func-useinterval) calls a function every period on the UI thread, and [`UseGo`](#func-usego) runs a function on its own goroutine with a context that is cancelled when its dependencies change or the component unmounts.
- [`UseMemo`](#func-usememo) caches a computation and [`UseOnce`](#func-useonce) computes a value once; [`UseCallback`](#func-usecallback) gives a stable [`Callback`](#type-callback) that always calls the latest function; [`UseRef`](#func-useref) keeps a mutable box.
- [`CreateContext`](#func-createcontext) and [`UseContext`](#func-usecontext) pass values down the tree.
- [`UseId`](#func-useid) gives a stable unique ID.
- [`UseElementRef`](#func-useelementref) gives an [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref) to attach with h.Ref, to focus or scroll an element from handlers and effects.
- [`UseValue`](#func-usevalue) holds an observable [`Value`](#type-value) for what changes every frame: read in the component's body, a change builds it again; read inside a deferred style closure, a change only lays out or repaints that element.
- [`UseScroll`](#func-usescroll) gives Values that follow an element's scroll offsets, for effects tied to scrolling that repaint without rebuilding.
- [`UseBounds`](#func-usebounds) gives a Value of an element's bounds in the window (a [`Rect`](#type-rect), moved by scrolling and transforms), a ResizeObserver that also sees position; in a handler, [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref).Bounds reads them.

### Scrolling

An element with overflow-auto or overflow-scroll (per axis: overflow-x-\*, overflow-y-\*) scrolls with the wheel, the touchpad (with a kinetic fling when the fingers lift), touch, the keyboard (arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End, Space) and its scrollbars; overflow-hidden scrolls only from code. The window itself scrolls like a browser page when the content is taller or wider than it ([`App`](#type-app).RootClass "overflow-hidden" turns that off); h-screen and h-full on the outer element still mean the window's height. Wheel scrolling chains to the scrolling ancestors at an edge unless overscroll-contain stops it. Scrollbars are thin overlay bars that appear while scrolling; [`App`](#type-app).ClassicScrollbars (or the class scrollbar-classic) draws always-visible classic bars that take space. User scrolling animates; [`App`](#type-app).InstantScroll (or scroll-instant on an element) turns animation and flings off, scroll-smooth turns them back on, and the system's reduced-motion setting always does. Code scrolls with [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref)'s ScrollTo, ScrollBy and ScrollIntoView (animated with scroll-smooth, like CSS), and h.OnScroll and h.OnWheel observe it:

```go
list := tela.UseElementRef()
_, y := tela.UseScroll(list)
header := Div(Class("h-16 bg-white shadow"), Style(tela.OpacityFn(func() float32 {
    return 1 - min(y.Get()/200, 1) // repaints only
})))
return Div(Class("flex h-screen flex-col"), header,
    Div(Ref(list), Class("grow overflow-y-auto"), rows),
    Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { list.ScrollTo(0, 0) }), Text("Top")))
```

Long lists use h.VirtualList, which builds only the rows in view, keeps the scroll position stable while rows of unknown height are measured, and scrolls to a row with [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref)'s ScrollToIndex and a [`ScrollAlign`](#type-scrollalign).

Text can be deferred the same way with h.TextFn: a Value read inside it lays out only the paragraph that holds the text, without building the component (a clock, a time label next to a seek bar).

A Value moved from a handler or a goroutine repaints only the element whose closure reads it:

```go
pos := tela.UseValue(float32(0)) // UseValue(0.0) would hold a float64
Div(Class("size-8 rounded-full bg-indigo-500"),
    Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (x, y float32) { return pos.Get(), 0 })))
// later, from anywhere: pos.Set(120)
```

Hooks follow React's rules: call them at the top level of a component function, in the same order on every build, never inside conditions or loops. A hook called outside a component build panics with an explanation (a component called where a node is expected is told to use [`C`](#func-c)); in dev mode a change of the hook order panics with both call sites. Everything runs on the UI thread except the Setter, Dispatcher and Value methods and [`Post`](#func-post), which are safe from any goroutine.

### Dev mode

Dev mode reports the mistakes that compile. It is on unless the program is a release build (built with -trimpath, or installed with go install pkg@version; go run and go build in a source checkout are development builds); [`App`](#type-app).Dev overrides that, and TELA_DEV=1 or TELA_DEV=0 overrides both. telatest runs in dev mode unless telatest.NoDev says otherwise. In dev mode:

- unknown classes are printed on standard error with the closest class (in telatest they fail the test);
- unknown roles, input types and easings, hook-order changes and hooks called outside their component panic with the fix;
- likely mistakes are printed as warnings, once per call site: lists without keys or with duplicate keys, UseEffect(f, nil) (deprecated: use [`UseMount`](#func-usemount)), dependencies that cannot be compared, a [`Value`](#type-value) read with Get in a handler while changes are queued (use Latest), a context read without a Provider whose default is not safe to use, and an h.Label that labels no field.

### Text fields and forms

h.Input and h.Textarea are editable text fields with the editing, selection, clipboard, undo and IME behavior of a browser's; h.Form submits on Enter or a submit button (h.OnSubmit), and h.Label names and focuses its field. Their events are [`ChangeEvent`](#type-changeevent) (every edit, React's onChange), [`InputEvent`](#type-inputevent) (before an edit, cancelable), [`CompositionEvent`](#type-compositionevent), [`SelectEvent`](#type-selectevent) and [`SubmitEvent`](#type-submitevent); [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref) reads and selects their text (Value, Select, SetSelectionRange, SelectionRange). See fields.go for an example.

### Snapshots and inspection

A package that defines `func Preview() tela.Node`, or a [`Previews`](#type-previews) variable, can be rendered headlessly with `tela snapshot`, and `tela inspect` prints its semantics tree as a Playwright aria snapshot (roles, names and states set by the h.Role and h.Aria... props or implied by the elements) or, with --layout, its layout tree. See the documentation of cmd/tela.

### Stability

[`Node`](#type-node), [`Child`](#type-child), [`Prop`](#type-prop), [`StyleProp`](#type-styleprop), [`Color`](#type-color), [`Shadow`](#type-shadow), [`Gradient`](#type-gradient), [`GradientStop`](#type-gradientstop), [`Setter`](#type-setter), [`Dispatcher`](#type-dispatcher), [`Callback`](#type-callback), [`Ref`](#type-ref), [`Context`](#type-context), [`Value`](#type-value), [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref), [`Rect`](#type-rect), [`ScrollAlign`](#type-scrollalign), [`MouseEvent`](#type-mouseevent), [`PointerEvent`](#type-pointerevent), [`DragEvent`](#type-dragevent), [`KeyboardEvent`](#type-keyboardevent), [`FocusEvent`](#type-focusevent), [`WheelEvent`](#type-wheelevent), [`ScrollEvent`](#type-scrollevent), [`InputEvent`](#type-inputevent), [`ChangeEvent`](#type-changeevent), [`CompositionEvent`](#type-compositionevent), [`SelectEvent`](#type-selectevent), [`SubmitEvent`](#type-submitevent), [`Key`](#type-key), [`Code`](#type-code), [`KeyLocation`](#type-keylocation), [`MouseButton`](#type-mousebutton), [`MouseButtons`](#type-mousebuttons) and [`PointerKind`](#type-pointerkind) are aliases of types defined in Tela's internal packages (the packages cannot be imported, but their exported fields and methods are part of the API shown here). Construct them with the functions of this package rather than with composite literals where one exists.

## Constants

```go
const (
    // MouseButtonNone is no button, as in a move or enter event.
    MouseButtonNone = core.MouseButtonNone
    // MouseButtonLeft is the primary button: the left button (the right
    // one on a left-handed setup), a touch contact or a pen tip.
    MouseButtonLeft = core.MouseButtonLeft
    // MouseButtonRight is the secondary button.
    MouseButtonRight = core.MouseButtonRight
    // MouseButtonMiddle is the wheel button.
    MouseButtonMiddle = core.MouseButtonMiddle
    // MouseButtonBack is the "back" side button.
    MouseButtonBack = core.MouseButtonBack
    // MouseButtonForward is the "forward" side button.
    MouseButtonForward = core.MouseButtonForward
)
```

The mouse buttons.

```go
const (
    PointerMouse = core.PointerMouse // a mouse or touchpad cursor
    PointerTouch = core.PointerTouch // a finger on a touchscreen
    PointerPen   = core.PointerPen   // a stylus
)
```

The pointer kinds.

```go
const (
    // KeyLocationStandard is every key not listed below.
    KeyLocationStandard = core.KeyLocationStandard
    // KeyLocationLeft is the left Shift, Control, Alt or Meta key.
    KeyLocationLeft = core.KeyLocationLeft
    // KeyLocationRight is the right Shift, Control, Alt (AltGr) or Meta key.
    KeyLocationRight = core.KeyLocationRight
    // KeyLocationNumpad is a key of the numeric keypad.
    KeyLocationNumpad = core.KeyLocationNumpad
)
```

The key locations (the DOM's KeyboardEvent.location).

```go
const (
    // AlignAuto scrolls as little as possible: not at all when the item
    // is fully visible, else to align its bottom (when it reaches past
    // the bottom of the viewport) or its top.
    AlignAuto = core.AlignAuto
    // AlignStart puts the item's top at the top of the viewport.
    AlignStart = core.AlignStart
    // AlignCenter centers the item in the viewport.
    AlignCenter = core.AlignCenter
    // AlignEnd puts the item's bottom at the bottom of the viewport.
    AlignEnd = core.AlignEnd
)
```

The alignments of [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref).ScrollToIndex. The first and last items include the list's padding: AlignStart on item 0 scrolls to the very top, AlignEnd on the last item to the very bottom.

## Variables

```go
var (
    // Transparent is fully transparent black.
    Transparent = gfx.Transparent
    // Black is opaque black.
    Black = gfx.Black
    // White is opaque white.
    White = gfx.White
)
```

Common colors.

## Functions

### func Animate

```go
func Animate[T Animatable](v *Value[T], target T, opts ...AnimationOption)
```

Animate moves v to target: with a spring by default (Motion's default, or as [`Stiffness`](#func-stiffness), [`Damping`](#func-damping), [`Bounce`](#func-bounce) or [`Spring`](#func-spring) say), or with a tween when the options are [`Duration`](#func-duration) and [`Ease`](#func-ease) only. v is any [`Value`](#type-value) of an [`Animatable`](#type-animatable) type, from [`UseValue`](#func-usevalue), [`UseSpring`](#func-usespring) or [`UseTween`](#func-usetween).

```go
y := tela.UseValue[float32](0)
Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { tela.Animate(y, 200, tela.Spring(tela.Bounce(0.25))) }),
    Text("Drop"))
tela.Animate(y, 0, tela.Duration(300*time.Millisecond), tela.Ease("ease-in-out"))
```

A new Animate on the same Value interrupts the running animation: the new one starts where the value is and, for a spring, at the speed it has, so a fling continues smoothly; a Set or Update of the Value stops the animation. Like Set, Animate is safe from any goroutine: the animation starts when the UI thread applies it, in order with the Value's Set and Update calls (an animation applied between two frames starts at the next one). Value.Latest does not anticipate animations: it returns the value they have reached.

With reduced motion, or in a tree that no frame clock drives, the value jumps to target. An animation of a Value whose component unmounts ends.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var y *tela.Value[float32]
ball := func() tela.Node {
    y = tela.UseValue[float32](0)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { tela.Animate(y, 200, tela.Spring(tela.Bounce(0.25))) }), Text("Drop")),
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) {
            tela.Animate(y, 0, tela.Duration(300*time.Millisecond), tela.Ease("ease-in-out"))
        }), Text("Lift")),
        Div(Class("size-8 rounded-full bg-indigo-500"), Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return 0, y.Get() }))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(ball))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Drop")) // settles: the spring ends
fmt.Println(y.Get())
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Lift"))
fmt.Println(y.Get())
// Output:
// 200
// 0
```

### func Assets

```go
func Assets(fsys fs.FS)
```

Assets registers a file system that background images are loaded from: the path in a class such as bg-\[url(img/hero.jpg)\] names a file of fsys, relative to its root (a leading "/" or "./" is ignored, so url(/img/hero.jpg) is the same file; ".." is not allowed). Call it from an init function, so that the files are found the same way by [`Run`](#func-run), tela snapshot, tela inspect and telatest:

```go
//go:embed img
var images embed.FS

func init() { tela.Assets(images) }
```

Assets may be called several times: the file systems are searched in the order they were registered and the first one that has the file wins. Files are decoded once, when first painted, and kept for the life of the process: PNG, JPEG, GIF (the first frame) and WebP, recognized by their content. A missing or undecodable file paints nothing and is reported once in the dev log, with the path and the registered file systems, like an unknown class. Remote and data: URLs are not supported.

**Example**

```go
// An app embeds its images and registers them from an init function:
//
//	//go:embed img
//	var images embed.FS
//
//	func init() { tela.Assets(images) }
//
// Here an in-memory file system holds one red PNG.
tela.Assets(fstest.MapFS{"img/red.png": {Data: solidPNG(color.RGBA{R: 255, A: 255})}})

// With package h: Div(Class("size-8 bg-[url(img/red.png)] bg-cover")).
card := core.Primitive(style.KindDiv, core.Class("size-8 bg-[url(img/red.png)] bg-cover"))
_, img := core.Render(card, core.RenderOptions{Width: 32, Height: 32})
fmt.Println(img.RGBAAt(16, 16))
// Output: {255 0 0 255}
```

### func Main

```go
func Main(app App)
```

Main runs app with [`Run`](#func-run) and, when Run returns an error (no display, for example), prints it on standard error and exits with status 1. It is the usual body of main:

```go
func main() {
    tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Demo", Width: 800, Height: 600, Root: Counter})
}
```

Main returns when the window is closed. Like Run, it must be called from the main goroutine, and it panics when app.Root is nil.

**Example**

```go
counter := func() tela.Node {
    count, setCount := tela.UseState(0)
    return Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setCount.Set(count + 1) }), Textf("Clicked %d times", count))
}
// In package main. Main returns when the window is closed; without a
// display it prints the error and exits with status 1.
tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Demo", Width: 400, Height: 300, Root: counter})
```

### func Post

```go
func Post(fn func())
```

Post runs fn on the UI thread of the running application, in order with the state updates queued before and after it. It is safe from any goroutine; use it to touch UI-thread state (a [`Ref`](#type-ref), a [`Callback`](#type-callback)'s forwarder) from background work.

```go
go func() {
    data := fetch()
    tela.Post(func() { cache.Current = data })
}()
```

Functions posted before [`Run`](#func-run) starts run once its window is up. Headless trees (tests, snapshots) do not run posted functions unless they receive them (telatest.Mount does); until then they wait, in order.

### func Run

```go
func Run(app App) error
```

Run opens a window, shows app.Root and runs the event loop until the window is closed. It must be called from the main goroutine, normally from main. The window is drawn by Tela's own renderer on the native backend: Wayland or X11 on Linux, Win32 and Cocoa elsewhere.

Run returns an error when the platform cannot open a window (for example, no display is available). It panics when app.Root is nil. [`Main`](#func-main) runs it and handles the error.

### func SetColorScheme

```go
func SetColorScheme(s ColorScheme)
```

SetColorScheme sets the color scheme of the running app: [`Light`](#type-colorscheme) or [`Dark`](#type-colorscheme) override the system's preference, [`System`](#type-colorscheme) follows it again. Every element is styled again (dark: classes) and the components that call [`UseColorScheme`](#func-usecolorscheme) build again. It is safe from any goroutine, like a state setter: the change applies on the UI thread before the next frame. Called before [`Run`](#func-run), it applies when the window opens (it wins over [`App`](#type-app).ColorScheme). Like [`Post`](#func-post), it goes to the app that receives posted functions (telatest.Mount's app in tests).

```go
Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { tela.SetColorScheme(tela.Dark) }), Text("Dark"))
```

It panics for a value other than System, Light and Dark.

**Example**

```go
toggle := func() tela.Node {
    dark := tela.UseColorScheme() == tela.Dark
    next, label := tela.Dark, "Dark mode"
    if dark {
        next, label = tela.Light, "Light mode"
    }
    return Button(Class("bg-white text-black dark:bg-black dark:text-white"),
        OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { tela.SetColorScheme(next) }), Text(label))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(toggle))
defer app.Close()
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Dark mode"))
fmt.Println(app.AriaSnapshot())
// Output:
// - button "Light mode"
```

### func SetTheme

```go
func SetTheme(t Theme)
```

SetTheme replaces the theme of the running app: classes are compiled again against it (with the app's ClassAliases), every element is styled again and the components that call [`UseTheme`](#func-usetheme) build again. Like [`SetColorScheme`](#func-setcolorscheme) it is safe from any goroutine, applies on the UI thread before the next frame, goes to the app that receives posted functions, and called before [`Run`](#func-run) applies when the window opens (it wins over [`App`](#type-app).Theme). It panics for a token name classes cannot use.

### func UseContext

```go
func UseContext[T any](ctx *Context[T]) T
```

UseContext returns the value of the nearest Provider of ctx above the component, or the context's default when there is none.

```go
theme := tela.UseContext(Theme)
```

In dev mode, reading a context without a Provider above warns (once per context) when its default is not safe to use: nil, or holding a nil function, pointer, map, channel or interface, or a zero [`Setter`](#type-setter) or [`Callback`](#type-callback), in an exported field. Either provide the context above every reader, or give CreateContext a default that works; IsZero tells a zero Setter or Callback apart where a missing Provider is expected.

### func UseEffect

```go
func UseEffect(effect func() func(), deps ...any)
```

UseEffect runs effect after the frame is presented, when its dependencies changed since the previous build. effect may return a cleanup function (or nil), which runs before the effect runs again and when the component unmounts.

The dependencies follow React:

```go
tela.UseEffect(f)          // after every build
tela.UseEffect(f, id, n)   // when id or n changed (compared with ==)
tela.UseMount(f)           // only after the first build (React's [])
```

For an effect that runs once, on mount, with its cleanup on unmount (a subscription), use [`UseMount`](#func-usemount); [`UseEffectDo`](#func-useeffectdo) takes an effect without a cleanup, [`UseUpdateEffect`](#func-useupdateeffect) skips the first build, and periodic and background work have [`UseInterval`](#func-useinterval) and [`UseGo`](#func-usego). A single nil dependency, UseEffect(f, nil), still means "only on mount", but it is deprecated (React reads a null list as "after every render"): dev mode warns about it, and a later version will reject it.

Values that cannot be compared (functions, slices, maps) count as changed on every build; dev mode reports them, and a dependency count that changes between builds. Pass an ID, a comparable value or a [`Callback`](#type-callback) instead.

Within a frame, the effects of children run before their parents', and every cleanup runs before the effects that follow it. Effects of a component whose build was skipped do not run. State set by an effect is applied in a later frame.

### func UseEffectDo

```go
func UseEffectDo(f func(), deps ...any)
```

UseEffectDo is [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect) for an effect without a cleanup: f runs after the frame is presented when the dependencies changed.

```go
tela.UseEffectDo(func() { title.Set(fmt.Sprintf("%d unread", n)) }, n)
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var title string
inbox := func() tela.Node {
    unread, setUnread := tela.UseState(3)
    tela.UseEffectDo(func() { title = fmt.Sprintf("Inbox (%d)", unread) }, unread)
    return Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setUnread.Set(0) }), Text("Mark all read"))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(inbox))
fmt.Println(title)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Mark all read"))
fmt.Println(title)
// Output:
// Inbox (3)
// Inbox (0)
```

### func UseGo

```go
func UseGo(f func(ctx context.Context), deps ...any)
```

UseGo runs f on a goroutine of its own after the frame is presented, when its dependencies changed, like [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect); ctx is cancelled at cleanup, when the dependencies change again or the component unmounts, before the next run starts. f must return soon after ctx is done (it is not waited for) and must change the UI only through what is safe from any goroutine: a [`Setter`](#type-setter), a [`Value`](#type-value), [`Post`](#func-post).

```go
tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
    for page := range fetchPages(ctx, query) {
        setResults.Update(func(r []Result) []Result { return append(r, page...) })
    }
}, query) // restarts, cancelling the old fetch, when query changes
```

The dependencies follow UseEffect's: none restarts f after every build.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
search := func(ctx context.Context, q string) []string {
    return []string{q + " one", q + " two"} // a slow call that honors ctx
}
results := func() tela.Node {
    query, setQuery := tela.UseState("tela")
    found, setFound := tela.UseState([]string(nil))
    tela.UseGo(func(ctx context.Context) {
        r := search(ctx, query)
        if ctx.Err() == nil { // a newer query cancelled this one
            setFound.Set(r) // safe from any goroutine
        }
    }, query)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setQuery.Set("go") }), Text("Search go")),
        Map(found, func(s string) tela.Node { return P(Key(s), Text(s)) }),
    )
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(results))
app.ExpectText("tela two") // expectations wait for the goroutine
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Search go"))
app.ExpectText("go one")
fmt.Println("ok")
// Output: ok
```

### func UseId

```go
func UseId() string
```

UseId returns a string that identifies this hook slot, for accessibility relations between elements (a label and its input). It is the same on every build, unique within the process, and the same for the same mount order (snapshots are deterministic).

```go
id := tela.UseId()
```

### func UseInterval

```go
func UseInterval(d time.Duration, f func())
```

UseInterval calls f on the UI thread every d, the first time d after the frame that first shows the component, until it unmounts. d \<= 0 pauses it, and a new d restarts it. f is always the latest build's function, so it sees the latest state and needs no dependencies. It runs on the window's frame clock, like the long-press timer, with no goroutine: telatest's App.Advance moves it, and a headless Render never runs it.

```go
now, setNow := tela.UseState(time.Now())
tela.UseInterval(time.Second, func() { setNow.Set(time.Now()) })
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
timer := func() tela.Node {
    seconds, setSeconds := tela.UseState(0)
    running, setRunning := tela.UseState(true)
    period := time.Second
    if !running {
        period = 0 // paused
    }
    tela.UseInterval(period, func() { setSeconds.Set(seconds + 1) })
    return Div(
        P(Textf("%d s", seconds)),
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setRunning.Set(!running) }), Text("Pause")),
    )
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(timer))
app.Advance(3 * time.Second) // the interval runs on the app's clock
app.ExpectText("3 s")
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Pause"))
app.Advance(5 * time.Second)
app.ExpectText("3 s")
fmt.Println("ok")
// Output: ok
```

### func UseLayoutEffect

```go
func UseLayoutEffect(effect func() func(), deps ...any)
```

UseLayoutEffect is [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect), but the effect runs in the frame after layout and before paint, with the same dependencies and cleanups. Its state updates are applied in the next frame.

```go
tela.UseLayoutEffect(func() func() {
    list.ScrollIntoView() // before the frame with the new item is painted
    return nil
}, len(items))
```

### func UseMemo

```go
func UseMemo[T any](compute func() T, deps ...any) T
```

UseMemo returns compute(), computed on the first build and again only when the dependencies changed (compared like [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect)'s: none recomputes on every build). For a value computed once, use [`UseOnce`](#func-useonce).

```go
visible := tela.UseMemo(func() []Todo { return filter(todos, query) }, len(todos), query)
```

### func UseMount

```go
func UseMount(effect func() func())
```

UseMount runs effect once, after the frame that first shows the component, and the cleanup it returns (nil for none) when the component unmounts: the idiom for subscriptions, listeners and other setup that lives as long as the component (React's useEffect(f, \[\])).

```go
tela.UseMount(func() func() {
    unsubscribe := store.Subscribe(func(s State) { setState.Set(s) })
    return unsubscribe
})
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var events []string
panel := func() tela.Node {
    tela.UseMount(func() func() {
        events = append(events, "subscribe")
        return func() { events = append(events, "unsubscribe") }
    })
    return Text("Panel")
}
page := func() tela.Node {
    open, setOpen := tela.UseState(true)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setOpen.Set(!open) }), Text("Toggle")),
        If(open, tela.C(panel)),
    )
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(page))
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Toggle")) // unmounts the panel
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Toggle")) // mounts it again
fmt.Println(events)
// Output: [subscribe unsubscribe subscribe]
```

### func UseOnce

```go
func UseOnce[T any](init func() T) T
```

UseOnce returns init(), called on the first build only; later builds return the same value. Use it for what a component creates once and keeps: a client, a buffer, the state struct of a custom hook. It is [`UseMemo`](#func-usememo) without dependencies; the value is not reactive (store what changes in [`UseState`](#func-usestate) or [`UseValue`](#func-usevalue)).

```go
cache := tela.UseOnce(func() map[string]Image { return map[string]Image{} })
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
created := 0
type cache struct{ hits map[string]int }
page := func() tela.Node {
    c := tela.UseOnce(func() *cache { created++; return &cache{hits: map[string]int{}} })
    n, setN := tela.UseState(0)
    c.hits["build"]++
    return Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setN.Set(n + 1) }), Textf("Add %d", n))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(page))
app.Click(telatest.ByText("Add"))
app.Click(telatest.ByText("Add"))
fmt.Println("created", created, "times")
// Output: created 1 times
```

### func UsePresence

```go
func UsePresence() (present bool, done func())
```

UsePresence reports whether the component is present, for a component inside a child of an h.Presence: present is false while that child exits, after it was removed. The component then runs its own exit (an [`Animate`](#func-animate), saving a draft...) and calls done when it is finished; the child unmounts once every component that used UsePresence called done and the transitions of its h.Exit classes ended. done is the same function on every build, safe from any goroutine, and does nothing while the component is present (a call from a previous exit that was cancelled is ignored). Outside any Presence, present is always true.

A toast that slides down and fades out before it unmounts: the tween to its exit position calls done when it arrives ([`OnDone`](#func-ondone); done does nothing while the toast is present, so the entrance may pass it too).

```go
func Toast(msg string) tela.Node {
    present, done := tela.UsePresence()
    target := float32(0)
    if !present {
        target = 1
    }
    out := tela.UseTween(float32(0), target, tela.Duration(200*time.Millisecond), tela.OnDone(done))
    return Div(Class("rounded-lg bg-slate-900 px-4 py-2 text-white"),
        Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return 0, 40 * out.Get() }),
            tela.OpacityFn(func() float32 { return 1 - out.Get() })),
        Text(msg))
}

Presence(If(saved, tela.C(func() tela.Node { return Toast("Saved") })))
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
toast := func() tela.Node {
    present, done := tela.UsePresence()
    target := float32(0)
    if !present {
        target = 1
    }
    // The tween out ends the exit: done does nothing while present.
    out := tela.UseTween(float32(0), target, tela.Duration(200*time.Millisecond), tela.OnDone(done))
    return Div(Role("status"), Class("rounded-lg bg-slate-900 px-4 py-2 text-white"),
        Style(tela.OpacityFn(func() float32 { return 1 - out.Get() })), Text("Saved"))
}
page := func() tela.Node {
    shown, setShown := tela.UseState(true)
    return Div(
        Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setShown.Set(false) }), Text("Dismiss")),
        Presence(If(shown, tela.C(toast))))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(page))
start := app.Now()
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Dismiss")) // waits for the exit
fmt.Println(app.Count(telatest.ByRole("status", "")), app.Now()-start >= 200*time.Millisecond)
// Output: 0 true
```

### func UseReducedMotion

```go
func UseReducedMotion() bool
```

UseReducedMotion reports whether the system asks for reduced motion (the motion-reduce: classes apply, transitions take no time and scrolling jumps). The component builds again when it changes. It is a hook: call it at the top level of a component.

**Example**

```go
spinner := func() tela.Node {
    if tela.UseReducedMotion() {
        return P(Text("Loading…"))
    }
    return Div(Class("size-6 animate-spin rounded-full border-2 border-t-transparent"), AriaLabel("Loading"), Role("status"))
}
yaml, _ := telatest.AriaSnapshot(tela.C(spinner), telatest.ReducedMotion())
fmt.Println(yaml)
// Output:
// - paragraph: Loading…
```

### func UseStateSet

```go
func UseStateSet[T any](initial T) (T, func(T))
```

UseStateSet is [`UseState`](#func-usestate) for those who only set whole values: it returns the Setter's Set method as a plain function, made once per slot.

```go
name, setName := tela.UseStateSet("")
setName("Ada")
```

It exists for code that wants React's shape, a setter that is a function: to pass it where a func(T) is expected (a callback of a library, a field's handler) without wrapping it, and to keep code ported from React reading the same. The function is the same on every build, but funcs are not comparable in Go, so a props struct holding one makes [`CP`](#func-cp) rebuild its component every time; pass the [`Setter`](#type-setter) of UseState in props instead.

### func UseStateUpdate

```go
func UseStateUpdate[T any](initial T) (T, func(func(T) T))
```

UseStateUpdate is [`UseState`](#func-usestate) for those who only update from the previous state: it returns the Setter's Update method as a plain function, made once per slot, for the same reasons as [`UseStateSet`](#func-usestateset).

```go
count, update := tela.UseStateUpdate(0)
update(func(n int) int { return n + 1 })
```

### func UseUpdateEffect

```go
func UseUpdateEffect(effect func() func(), deps ...any)
```

UseUpdateEffect is [`UseEffect`](#func-useeffect) without the run of the first build: the effect runs after the later builds whose dependencies changed (react-use's useUpdateEffect), and its cleanup before it runs again and on unmount. Use it to react to changes, not to the initial value.

```go
tela.UseUpdateEffect(func() func() {
    save(settings) // not on mount, only when settings change
    return nil
}, settings)
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var saved []string
editor := func() tela.Node {
    theme, setTheme := tela.UseState("light")
    tela.UseUpdateEffect(func() func() {
        saved = append(saved, theme) // not on mount: only changes are saved
        return nil
    }, theme)
    return Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { setTheme.Set("dark") }), Text("Dark"))
}
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(editor))
fmt.Println(saved)
app.Click(telatest.ByRole("button", "Dark"))
fmt.Println(saved)
// Output:
// []
// [dark]
```

## Types

### type Animatable

```go
type Animatable = core.Animatable
```

Animatable lists the types that [`UseSpring`](#func-usespring), [`UseTween`](#func-usetween) and [`Animate`](#func-animate) animate:

- float32: a number (an offset, a scale, an opacity, a progress);
- [`Color`](#type-color): interpolated as CSS transitions interpolate colors, premultiplied by alpha, in sRGB between two colors written as hex, rgb() or named colors, and in Oklab otherwise (the Oklch palette of Tailwind, [`OKLCH`](#func-oklch)); read it in a [`BgFn`](#func-bgfn) or [`TextColorFn`](#func-textcolorfn) to animate a color by repainting only;
- [`Point`](#type-point), [`Size`](#type-size) and [`Rect`](#type-rect): component by component, each with its own velocity.

`Animatable` is an alias of `core.Animatable`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Animatable interface {
    float32 | gfx.Color | Point | Size | Rect
}
```

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var bg *tela.Value[tela.Color]
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    bg = tela.UseValue(tela.Hex("#ffffff"))
    // Read in the paint phase: the animation only repaints the box.
    return Div(Class("size-10"), Style(tela.BgFn(bg.Get)))
}), telatest.NoSettle())
// Hex colors interpolate in sRGB, like a CSS transition between them.
tela.Animate(bg, tela.Hex("#000000"), tela.Duration(100*time.Millisecond), tela.Ease("linear"))
app.Advance(50 * time.Millisecond) // 33 ms of the tween: see ExamplePoint
fmt.Println(bg.Get())
// Output: #aaaaaa
```

### type AnimationOption

```go
type AnimationOption = core.AnimOption
```

AnimationOption configures an animation of [`UseSpring`](#func-usespring), [`UseTween`](#func-usetween) or [`Animate`](#func-animate): [`Stiffness`](#func-stiffness), [`Damping`](#func-damping), [`Bounce`](#func-bounce), [`Duration`](#func-duration), [`Ease`](#func-ease), [`Velocity`](#func-velocity) and [`Spring`](#func-spring), which groups spring options, and [`OnDone`](#func-ondone). The zero AnimationOption changes nothing.

Springs (Motion's model) are defined either by their physics or by how long they take:

```go
tela.Stiffness(300), tela.Damping(30)        // physics; mass 1
tela.Spring(tela.Duration(500*time.Millisecond), tela.Bounce(0.25))
```

Without options a spring has stiffness 100 and damping 10 (Motion's default, slightly bouncy); Bounce without a Duration takes 800 ms, and a Duration without Bounce a bounce of 0.3. Tweens take a [`Duration`](#func-duration) (default 300 ms) and an [`Ease`](#func-ease) (default CSS's "ease").

Options that contradict each other or the hook (Ease on a spring, Stiffness and Duration together, spring options on UseTween), invalid numbers and invalid easing strings panic in dev mode (see [`App`](#type-app).Dev) with what to write instead; otherwise they are ignored.

`AnimationOption` is an alias of `core.AnimOption`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type AnimOption struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

**Example**

```go
// Options for the three kinds of motion.
physics := []tela.AnimationOption{tela.Stiffness(300), tela.Damping(30)}
timed := []tela.AnimationOption{tela.Spring(tela.Duration(400*time.Millisecond), tela.Bounce(0.2))}
tween := []tela.AnimationOption{tela.Duration(250 * time.Millisecond), tela.Ease("cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)")}
fmt.Println(len(physics), len(timed), len(tween))
// Output: 2 1 2
```

#### func Bounce

```go
func Bounce(b float64) AnimationOption
```

Bounce sets how bouncy a spring defined by its duration is (Motion's bounce): 0 does not overshoot, 0.25 bounces a little, values toward 1 oscillate longer. Without a [`Duration`](#func-duration) the spring takes 800 ms. It makes [`Animate`](#func-animate) use a spring.

**Example**

```go
// A spring defined by its duration (800 ms without Duration) ends no
// earlier than it, at rest.
fmt.Println("bounce 0:", springEnd(tela.Spring(tela.Bounce(0))))
fmt.Println("bounce 0.5:", springEnd(tela.Spring(tela.Bounce(0.5))))
// Output:
// bounce 0: 830ms
// bounce 0.5: 870ms
```

#### func Damping

```go
func Damping(c float64) AnimationOption
```

Damping sets the damping of a spring: how strongly it resists motion (default 10). Low values bounce around the target; damping = 2\*sqrt(stiffness) is critically damped (no overshoot), so Stiffness(300) with Damping(35) settles without bouncing. It makes [`Animate`](#func-animate) use a spring.

**Example**

```go
// Damping 2*sqrt(stiffness) is critically damped: no overshoot. Less
// bounces around the target and takes longer to come to rest.
fmt.Println("damping 40:", springEnd(tela.Stiffness(400), tela.Damping(40)))
fmt.Println("damping 10:", springEnd(tela.Stiffness(400), tela.Damping(10)))
// Output:
// damping 40: 480ms
// damping 10: 1.15s
```

#### func Duration

```go
func Duration(d time.Duration) AnimationOption
```

Duration sets how long a tween takes, or, for a spring ([`UseSpring`](#func-usespring), or inside [`Spring`](#func-spring)), the time a spring found from it settles in (Motion's duration/bounce springs; it ends no earlier). A Duration of 0 jumps to the target: the value is stored at once, a tween's or a spring's, and an [`OnDone`](#func-ondone) is queued right after, as for any target that applies at once.

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println("tween:", springEnd(tela.Duration(250*time.Millisecond)))
fmt.Println("spring:", springEnd(tela.Spring(tela.Duration(250*time.Millisecond))))
// Output:
// tween: 270ms
// spring: 320ms
```

#### func Ease

```go
func Ease(css string) AnimationOption
```

Ease sets the easing curve of a tween, a CSS \<easing-function\>: one of the keywords linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, step-start and step-end, cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) or steps(n\[, position\]). The keywords are CSS's curves: Tailwind's ease-out utility is Ease("cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)"). An invalid string panics in dev mode with a suggestion (Ease("ease-out-cubic"): did you mean "ease-out"?); otherwise the tween uses "ease".

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println("ease-out:", springEnd(tela.Ease("ease-out"))) // 300 ms by default
fmt.Println("steps:", springEnd(tela.Duration(time.Second), tela.Ease("steps(4, jump-end)")))
// Output:
// ease-out: 320ms
// steps: 1.03s
```

#### func OnDone

```go
func OnDone(fn func()) AnimationOption
```

OnDone calls fn when the animation comes to rest at its target: once, on the UI thread, queued with the state updates like [`Post`](#func-post), so it runs before the next build and state it sets is built in the frame that shows the target. It is not called when the animation is interrupted: by another Animate, Set or Update of the Value, by a new target of [`UseSpring`](#func-usespring) or [`UseTween`](#func-usetween), or by the unmount of the Value's component. When the target applies at once (reduced motion, a tree that no frame clock drives, [`Duration`](#func-duration)(0), a value already at its target and at rest, a NaN target) fn is queued right after it applies. For UseSpring and UseTween it is the OnDone of the build that set the target that runs.

```go
tela.Animate(x, 0, tela.Spring(), tela.OnDone(func() { setOpen.Set(false) }))
```

It is how a component inside an h.Presence child ends its own exit: see [`UsePresence`](#func-usepresence).

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var x *tela.Value[float32]
var log []string
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    x = tela.UseValue[float32](0)
    return Div(Class("size-8 bg-black"), Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return x.Get(), 0 })))
}), telatest.NoSettle())
tela.Animate(x, 100, tela.OnDone(func() { log = append(log, "first") }))
app.Advance(50 * time.Millisecond)
// Interrupted: the first OnDone never runs.
tela.Animate(x, 0, tela.Duration(100*time.Millisecond), tela.OnDone(func() { log = append(log, "second") }))
app.Advance(time.Second)
fmt.Println(log, x.Get())
// Output: [second] 0
```

#### func Spring

```go
func Spring(opts ...AnimationOption) AnimationOption
```

Spring makes the animation a spring with the options given: [`Stiffness`](#func-stiffness) and [`Damping`](#func-damping), or [`Duration`](#func-duration) and [`Bounce`](#func-bounce). Spring() alone is Motion's default spring. It is how [`Animate`](#func-animate) gets a spring defined by its duration:

```go
tela.Animate(y, 200, tela.Spring(tela.Duration(400*time.Millisecond), tela.Bounce(0.3)))
```

**Example**

```go
fmt.Println("Motion's default:", springEnd(tela.Spring()))
fmt.Println("500 ms, bounce 0.3:", springEnd(tela.Spring(tela.Duration(500*time.Millisecond), tela.Bounce(0.3))))
// Output:
// Motion's default: 1.07s
// 500 ms, bounce 0.3: 530ms
```

#### func Stiffness

```go
func Stiffness(k float64) AnimationOption
```

Stiffness sets the stiffness of a spring: how strongly it pulls the value to its target (default 100). Higher is faster. With [`Damping`](#func-damping) it defines the spring by its physics, so it cannot be combined with [`Duration`](#func-duration) or [`Bounce`](#func-bounce). It makes [`Animate`](#func-animate) use a spring.

**Example**

```go
// Four times the stiffness (with the damping that keeps both critically
// damped) arrives in about half the time.
fmt.Println("stiffness 100:", springEnd(tela.Stiffness(100), tela.Damping(20)))
fmt.Println("stiffness 400:", springEnd(tela.Stiffness(400), tela.Damping(40)))
// Output:
// stiffness 100: 870ms
// stiffness 400: 480ms
```

#### func Velocity

```go
func Velocity[T Animatable](v T) AnimationOption
```

Velocity sets the initial velocity of a spring, in the Value's units per second, component by component (a [`Point`](#type-point)'s X and Y, a [`Rect`](#type-rect)'s X, Y, Width and Height). It replaces the velocity an interrupted animation would pass on: a released drag hands its pointer velocity to the spring that brings the element back:

```go
OnDragEnd(func(e tela.DragEvent) {
    tela.Animate(pos, tela.Point{}, tela.Spring(), tela.Velocity(tela.Point{X: e.VelocityX, Y: e.VelocityY}))
})
```

It makes [`Animate`](#func-animate) use a spring. Its type must be the Value's, and it does not apply to tweens ([`UseTween`](#func-usetween), or Duration and Ease alone) nor to [`Color`](#type-color) values, whose components move in a space (sRGB or Oklab, premultiplied) that depends on the two colors: those panic in dev mode and are ignored otherwise.

**Example**

```go
t := &exampleT{}
defer t.close()
var x *tela.Value[float32]
app := telatest.Mount(t, tela.C(func() tela.Node {
    x = tela.UseValue[float32](0)
    return Div(Class("size-8 bg-black"), Style(tela.TranslateFn(func() (float32, float32) { return x.Get(), 0 })))
}), telatest.NoSettle())
// A flick at rest: the value is already at its target, the velocity
// carries it away and the spring brings it back.
tela.Animate(x, 0, tela.Stiffness(200), tela.Damping(20), tela.Velocity(float32(600)))
var peak float32
for range 30 {
    app.Advance(time.Second / 60)
    peak = max(peak, x.Get())
}
app.Advance(2 * time.Second)
fmt.Printf("peak %.0f, rest %v\n", peak, x.Get())
// Output: peak 19, rest 0
```

### type App

```go
type App struct {
    // Title is the window title.
    Title string
    // AppID identifies the application to the desktop environment (the
    // Wayland app_id, the X11 WM_CLASS). Use a reverse-DNS name such as
    // "com.example.notes". Empty lets the platform pick one.
    AppID string
    // Width and Height are the requested size of the window in logical
    // pixels. Zero means the platform's default size.
    Width, Height float32
    // RootClass are Tailwind classes for the root, which fills the
    // window. Use it to give the window a background ("bg-slate-900") or
    // a text style; without it the window is white and the text black.
    // The root is the viewport: content taller or wider than the window
    // scrolls, unless RootClass sets an overflow ("overflow-hidden" keeps
    // the window from scrolling; CSS's overflow propagation).
    RootClass string
    // Root is the root component. It is built as a component of its own,
    // so it may use hooks.
    Root func() Node
    // ClassicScrollbars draws always-visible classic scrollbars (a
    // Windows look) that take space next to the content, instead of the
    // default thin overlay bars that appear while scrolling. The classes
    // scrollbar-classic and scrollbar-overlay choose per element.
    ClassicScrollbars bool
    // InstantScroll makes wheel, keyboard and scrollbar scrolling jump
    // instead of animating, and touchpad and touch scrolling stop when
    // the fingers lift instead of flinging. Elements with scroll-smooth
    // still animate; the class scroll-instant does the same for one
    // element.
    InstantScroll bool
    // ColorScheme is the app's color scheme: Light or Dark override the
    // system's preference (the dark: classes, UseColorScheme); the zero
    // value, System, follows it. SetColorScheme changes it while the app
    // runs.
    ColorScheme ColorScheme
    // Theme holds the color tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground),
    // the base radius and the fonts of the app; nil means DefaultTheme,
    // so the shadcn/ui tokens always resolve. SetTheme changes it while
    // the app runs. See [Theme].
    Theme *Theme
    // ClassAliases are class names that stand for class strings, for the
    // combinations an app repeats:
    //
    //	ClassAliases: map[string]string{
    //	    "text-muted": "text-sm text-muted-foreground",
    //	    "card-title": "text-lg font-semibold dark:text-white",
    //	}
    //
    // An alias expands where it appears, so later classes still win over
    // its classes and its classes over earlier ones. Its variants apply
    // to every class of the expansion: "hover:card-title" is "hover:text-lg
    // hover:font-semibold hover:dark:text-white". An alias may use other
    // aliases; a cycle is reported like an unknown class. An alias wins
    // over a class of the same name ("text-muted" is also the muted token
    // as a text color). A key is one class name without variants, spaces
    // or brackets; Run panics otherwise. Aliases are also suggested for
    // misspelled classes.
    ClassAliases map[string]string
    // Dev turns dev mode on or off. Dev mode reports the mistakes that
    // compile: unknown classes are printed on standard error; unknown
    // roles, input types and easings panic with the closest valid name;
    // hooks called in another order or outside their component panic
    // with the fix; likely mistakes (lists without keys, nil
    // dependencies, a Value read while changes are queued...) are printed
    // as warnings. It costs some speed.
    //
    // Nil, the default, means on unless the program is a release build:
    // go run and go build in a source checkout give development builds,
    // while a binary built with -trimpath, or installed with go install
    // pkg@version, is a release build. The environment variable
    // TELA_DEV=1 or TELA_DEV=0 overrides both Dev and the default.
    //
    //	off := false
    //	tela.Main(tela.App{Title: "Notes", Root: Notes, Dev: &off})
    Dev *bool
}
```

App describes an application window for [`Run`](#func-run).

```go
tela.Run(tela.App{
    Title:             "Files",
    Root:              Root,
    ClassicScrollbars: true, // always-visible classic bars (a Windows look)
    InstantScroll:     true, // no scroll animation, no inertia
})
```

### type Callback

```go
type Callback[F any] = core.Callback[F]
```

Callback is a stable handle on the latest function given to [`UseCallback`](#func-usecallback): cb.Fn() returns one forwarding function, the same on every build, that calls the latest function. It is comparable, so a props struct holding one stays comparable and [`CP`](#func-cp) can skip the component that receives it. The zero Callback is tied to no slot: Fn panics, and IsZero reports it, for optional callbacks in props:

```go
if !p.OnClose.IsZero() {
    p.OnClose.Fn()()
}
```

`Callback` is an alias of `core.Callback`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Callback[F any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

#### func UseCallback

```go
func UseCallback[F any](fn F) Callback[F]
```

UseCallback stores fn as the latest function of this hook slot and returns the slot's [`Callback`](#type-callback). cb.Fn() is one function of type F, the same on every build, that calls the latest fn when it is called (React's useEffectEvent): handlers keep a stable identity and still see the latest build's values. There are no dependencies. F must be a function type; UseCallback panics otherwise, and for a nil fn.

```go
onSave := tela.UseCallback(func(e tela.MouseEvent) { save(draft) })
return tela.CP(Toolbar, ToolbarProps{OnSave: onSave}) // skips while draft changes

// in Toolbar:
Button(OnClick(p.OnSave.Fn()), Text("Save"))
```

Call the forwarder on the UI thread (handlers and effects run there); from other goroutines, use [`Post`](#func-post).

#### func (Callback) Fn

```go
func (c Callback[F]) Fn() F
```

Fn returns the slot's forwarding function: one function of type F, the same on every build, that calls the latest function given to UseCallback at the time it is called. Call it on the UI thread (event handlers and effects run there); from other goroutines, use Post.

#### func (Callback) IsZero

```go
func (c Callback[F]) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether c is the zero Callback, which is not tied to any UseCallback slot: Fn panics. A Callback left unset in a props struct, or read from a context default without a Provider, is zero.

### type ChangeEvent

```go
type ChangeEvent = core.ChangeEvent
```

ChangeEvent is passed to h.OnChange after every edit of a text field's value, like React's onChange (the DOM's input event, not its change on blur): Value is the new value (with the text an IME is composing), InputType, Data and IsComposing describe the edit as in [`InputEvent`](#type-inputevent). It bubbles, so a Form's OnChange sees the edits of all its fields.

```go
name, setName := tela.UseState("")
Input(Value(name), OnChange(func(e tela.ChangeEvent) { setName.Set(e.Value) }))
// the same: Input(Bind(name, setName))
```

`ChangeEvent` is an alias of `core.ChangeEvent`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type ChangeEvent struct {
    Value       string
    InputType   string
    Data        string
    IsComposing bool
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

#### func (ChangeEvent) DefaultPrevented

```go
func (e ChangeEvent) DefaultPrevented() bool
```

DefaultPrevented reports whether a handler called PreventDefault.

#### func (ChangeEvent) PreventDefault

```go
func (e ChangeEvent) PreventDefault()
```

PreventDefault marks the event; the edit already happened.

#### func (ChangeEvent) StopPropagation

```go
func (e ChangeEvent) StopPropagation()
```

StopPropagation stops the event from bubbling (see MouseEvent).

### type Child

```go
type Child = core.Child
```

Child is what an element takes: a [`Node`](#type-node) (a child) or a [`Prop`](#type-prop) (h.Class, h.Style, h.Key, h.OnClick...). Props and children may be mixed in any order. The interface is sealed: passing a string or any other value is a compile error; wrap text in h.Text. The compiler names the internal type behind the alias and its unexported method:

```go
cannot use "hello" (constant of type string) as tela.Child value in
argument to Div: string does not implement core.Child (missing method
applyChild)
```

means Div("hello") should be Div(Text("hello")).

`Child` is an alias of `core.Child`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Child interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}
```

### type Code

```go
type Code = core.CodeValue
```

Code is a physical key: its position on the keyboard whatever the layout (a W3C KeyboardEvent code value), one of the Code constants. Use it for shortcuts that depend on the position (WASD), and Key for those that depend on the meaning (Ctrl+Z):

```go
if e.Code == tela.CodeKeyW || e.Code == "ArrowUp" { moveUp() }
```

`Code` is an alias of `core.CodeValue`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type CodeValue string
```

### type Color

```go
type Color = gfx.Color
```

Color is a non-premultiplied color with float32 components R, G, B and A. A (opacity) is in \[0, 1\]. R, G and B are extended sRGB, like CSS Color 4: they are in \[0, 1\] for colors inside the sRGB gamut, while a color outside it, such as a third of the Tailwind palette once converted from OKLCH, keeps components below 0 or above 1 and is clipped when painted, as browsers do. Clamp before converting to 8-bit values. The zero value is transparent black.

Color is an alias of an internal type: use its fields and methods (WithAlpha, MulAlpha, String...) and the constructors Hex, RGB, RGBA and OKLCH.

`Color` is an alias of `gfx.Color`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Color struct{ R, G, B, A float32 }
```

#### func Hex

```go
func Hex(s string) Color
```

Hex parses a CSS hex color: "#rgb", "#rgba", "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa". It panics with the reason when s is not valid, since a literal that does not parse is a programmer error.

```go
tela.Hex("#1e1e2e")
```

**Example**

```go
c := tela.Hex("#1e1e2e")
fmt.Println(c.R == tela.RGB(30, 30, 46).R, c)
// Output: true #1e1e2e
```

#### func OKLCH

```go
func OKLCH(l, c, h float32) Color
```

OKLCH returns the opaque color with OKLCH lightness l (0 to 1), chroma c (about 0 to 0.4) and hue h in degrees, the notation of the Tailwind v4 palette: tela.OKLCH(0.637, 0.237, 25.331) is red-500. Use WithAlpha for transparency. The result is not gamut-mapped (see [`Color`](#type-color)).

#### func RGB

```go
func RGB(r, g, b uint8) Color
```

RGB returns the opaque color with the given 8-bit components.

#### func RGBA

```go
func RGBA(r, g, b uint8, a float32) Color
```

RGBA returns the color with the given 8-bit components and an alpha from 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), like CSS rgba(r, g, b, a).

#### func (Color) Clamp

```go
func (c Color) Clamp() Color
```

Clamp returns c with every component clamped to \[0, 1\]. NaN becomes 0. For an extended sRGB color this per-channel clip is what browsers paint.

#### func (Color) IsFinite

```go
func (c Color) IsFinite() bool
```

IsFinite reports whether all four components are finite.

#### func (Color) IsOpaque

```go
func (c Color) IsOpaque() bool
```

IsOpaque reports whether A \>= 1.

#### func (Color) MulAlpha

```go
func (c Color) MulAlpha(f float32) Color
```

MulAlpha returns c with its alpha multiplied by f (Tailwind's "bg-white/15" is White.MulAlpha(0.15)).

#### func (Color) NRGBA8

```go
func (c Color) NRGBA8() color.NRGBA
```

NRGBA8 returns the non-premultiplied 8-bit color, rounded to nearest.

#### func (Color) Premul8

```go
func (c Color) Premul8() color.RGBA
```

Premul8 returns the premultiplied 8-bit color, with every channel rounded to nearest (half up) from the exact float value, never by premultiplying already-rounded bytes. The result satisfies R,G,B \<= A.

#### func (Color) Premultiplied

```go
func (c Color) Premultiplied() (r, g, b, a float32)
```

Premultiplied returns the premultiplied components (R\*A, G\*A, B\*A, A) as floats in \[0, 1\].

#### func (Color) String

```go
func (c Color) String() string
```

String returns "#rrggbb" for opaque colors and "#rrggbbaa" otherwise, with components rounded to 8 bits.

#### func (Color) ToOKLCH

```go
func (c Color) ToOKLCH() (l, ch, h float32)
```

ToOKLCH returns the OKLCH coordinates of c (alpha is ignored). The hue h is in degrees in \[0, 360); it is 0 for achromatic colors.

#### func (Color) ToOklab

```go
func (c Color) ToOklab() (l, a, b float32)
```

ToOklab returns the Oklab coordinates of c (alpha is ignored), extended sRGB components included. l is in \[0, 1\] for in-gamut colors; a and b are roughly in \[-0.4, 0.4\].

#### func (Color) WithAlpha

```go
func (c Color) WithAlpha(a float32) Color
```

WithAlpha returns c with its alpha replaced by a.

### type ColorScheme

```go
type ColorScheme = core.ColorScheme
```

ColorScheme is a color scheme: what the app asks for ([`System`](#type-colorscheme), [`Light`](#type-colorscheme) or [`Dark`](#type-colorscheme)) in [`App`](#type-app).ColorScheme and [`SetColorScheme`](#func-setcolorscheme), and the effective scheme [`UseColorScheme`](#func-usecolorscheme) returns ([`Light`](#type-colorscheme) or [`Dark`](#type-colorscheme)). The dark: classes apply in the effective [`Dark`](#type-colorscheme) scheme.

`ColorScheme` is an alias of `core.ColorScheme`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type ColorScheme uint8
```

```go
const (
    ColorSchemeSystem ColorScheme = iota
    ColorSchemeLight
    ColorSchemeDark
)// ColorSchemeSystem follows the system's preference (the zero
// value).
// ColorSchemeDark is the dark scheme: dark: variants apply.
```

```go
const (
    // System follows the system's light or dark preference. It is the
    // zero value, so an [App] follows the system unless it sets
    // ColorScheme.
    System ColorScheme = core.ColorSchemeSystem
    // Light is the light scheme: dark: classes do not apply.
    Light ColorScheme = core.ColorSchemeLight
    // Dark is the dark scheme: dark: classes apply.
    Dark ColorScheme = core.ColorSchemeDark
)
```

#### func UseColorScheme

```go
func UseColorScheme() ColorScheme
```

UseColorScheme returns the color scheme at the component's position, [`Light`](#type-colorscheme) or [`Dark`](#type-colorscheme): the one the nearest element above it with an h.Scheme prop gives, else the app's, the one the app set ([`App`](#type-app).ColorScheme, [`SetColorScheme`](#func-setcolorscheme)) or, with [`System`](#type-colorscheme), the system's preference. The component builds again when it changes, like with a state hook. It is a hook: call it at the top level of a component.

```go
func Logo() tela.Node {
    src := lightLogo
    if tela.UseColorScheme() == tela.Dark {
        src = darkLogo
    }
    return Img(SrcImage(src), Alt("Tela"))
}
```

Classes do not need it: dark:bg-slate-900 already follows the scheme.

**Example**

```go
theme := func() tela.Node {
    name := "light"
    if tela.UseColorScheme() == tela.Dark {
        name = "dark"
    }
    return P(Textf("Theme: %s", name))
}
// The system prefers dark (telatest.Dark), the app follows it.
yaml, _ := telatest.AriaSnapshot(tela.C(theme), telatest.Dark())
fmt.Println(yaml)
// The app overrides the system (tela.App.ColorScheme).
yaml, _ = telatest.AriaSnapshot(tela.C(theme), telatest.Dark(), telatest.ColorScheme(tela.Light))
fmt.Println(yaml)
// Output:
// - paragraph: "Theme: dark"
// - paragraph: "Theme: light"
```

#### func (ColorScheme) String

```go
func (s ColorScheme) String() string
```

### type Context

```go

```

Context passes a value down the tree without props: see [`CreateContext`](#func-createcontext).

`Context` is an alias of `core.Context`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

#### func CreateContext

```go
func CreateContext[T any](def T) *Context[T]
```

CreateContext returns a new context whose [`UseContext`](#func-usecontext) outside any Provider returns def. Create contexts once, at package level.

```go
var Theme = tela.CreateContext("light")

func App() tela.Node {
    theme, _ := tela.UseState("dark")
    return Theme.Provider(theme, tela.C(Page))
}
```

ctx.Provider(value, children...) returns a node without a box that gives value to its children's subtrees (only h.Key is accepted as a prop). When the Provider gets a value that is not == to the previous one (values that cannot be compared always count as changed), only the components that read it with UseContext build again, even when the components between them skip their build.

#### func (*Context) Provider

```go
func (c *Context[T]) Provider(value T, children ...Child) Node
```

Provider returns a node that gives value to the UseContext calls of its children's subtrees. It has no box: the children become children of the provider's parent, like a Fragment, and only Key is accepted as a prop.

### type Dispatcher

```go
type Dispatcher[A any] = core.Dispatcher[A]
```

Dispatcher sends actions to one [`UseReducer`](#func-usereducer) slot: d.Dispatch(action). Like [`Setter`](#type-setter), it is comparable, stable for its slot and safe from any goroutine.

`Dispatcher` is an alias of `core.Dispatcher`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type Dispatcher[A any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

#### func UseReducer

```go
func UseReducer[S, A any](reducer func(S, A) S, initial S) (S, Dispatcher[A])
```

UseReducer returns the state of this hook slot and a [`Dispatcher`](#type-dispatcher) whose actions update it with reducer (React's useReducer). The first build stores initial. Queued actions apply in order on the UI thread with the reducer of the latest build, each receiving the state left by the previous one; reducer must be pure. For comparable states, a result == to the current state does not rebuild.

```go
type action struct{ kind string }

func reduce(n int, a action) int {
    switch a.kind {
    case "inc":
        return n + 1
    case "reset":
        return 0
    }
    return n
}

count, d := tela.UseReducer(reduce, 0)
d.Dispatch(action{"inc"})
```

#### func (Dispatcher) Dispatch

```go
func (d Dispatcher[A]) Dispatch(a A)
```

Dispatch queues action a. When the update applies on the UI thread, the reducer of the latest build computes the new state from the state left by the previous queued update; for comparable states, a result == to the current state does not rebuild.

DragEvent is passed to h.OnDragStart, h.OnDrag and h.OnDragEnd: the position, the movement since the previous drag event (DeltaX, DeltaY) and since the press (OffsetX, OffsetY), and the velocity in pixels per second (VelocityX, VelocityY; meaningful at the end).

type DragEvent struct {
    // X and Y are the position in the window, LocalX and LocalY relative
    // to the border box of the element (see MouseEvent).
    X, Y, LocalX, LocalY float32
    // DeltaX and DeltaY are the movement since the previous drag event
    // (since the press for OnDragStart).
    DeltaX, DeltaY float32
    // OffsetX and OffsetY are the movement since the press: an element
    // moved by them follows the pointer exactly.
    OffsetX, OffsetY float32
    // VelocityX and VelocityY are the pointer velocity in logical pixels
    // per second, from the last 100 ms of moves; meaningful at
    // OnDragEnd (a fling), zero when the pointer stopped before the
    // release or the drag was cancelled.
    VelocityX, VelocityY float32
    // Button is the button of the drag (MouseButtonLeft).

    // Modifier keys held during the event.

    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}

### type ElementRef

```go
type ElementRef = core.ElementRef
```

ElementRef is a handle on the element it is attached to with h.Ref, returned by [`UseElementRef`](#func-useelementref): the same comparable value on every build. Its methods act on the element while it is mounted and do nothing (or report false) otherwise; call them from event handlers and effects.

- Focus focuses the element, if it is focusable (a Button, an h.Input or h.Textarea, or an element with h.TabIndex, not disabled or hidden).
- Blur removes the focus from the element if it has it.
- Focused reports whether the element has the focus of its window.
- ScrollTo(x, y) and ScrollBy(dx, dy) scroll a scrolling element (overflow auto, scroll or hidden) to or by offsets, clamped to its content; ScrollOffset returns its offsets (the DOM's scrollLeft and scrollTop). They jump, or animate when the element has scroll-smooth, and do nothing (or return 0) for other elements.
- ScrollIntoView scrolls every scrolling ancestor of the element so that it is visible, each as little as possible (block and inline "nearest").
- Bounds returns the element's border box in window coordinates as a [`Rect`](#type-rect), moved by scrolling and transforms (getBoundingClientRect); the zero Rect before it is laid out. [`UseBounds`](#func-usebounds) follows it in a [`Value`](#type-value).
- ScrollToIndex(i, align) scrolls an h.VirtualList to item i, placed as [`ScrollAlign`](#type-scrollalign) says, and keeps it there while the items around it are measured; it does nothing for other elements.
- Text fields (h.Input, h.Textarea): Value returns the value (the DOM's input.value: mainly for uncontrolled fields), Select selects all of it, SetSelectionRange(start, end) selects part of it and SelectionRange returns the selection, in UTF-8 byte offsets of the value (HTML's select(), setSelectionRange, selectionStart and selectionEnd); on other elements they do nothing and return "" or 0, 0.

For example, "/" focuses a search box:

```go
search := tela.UseElementRef()
return Div(OnKeyDown(func(e tela.KeyboardEvent) {
        if e.Key == "/" && !search.Focused() {
            e.PreventDefault()
            search.Focus()
            search.Select()
        }
    }),
    Input(Ref(search), Type("search"), Placeholder("Search"), Class("rounded-md border px-2 py-1")),
)
```

A "back to top" button for a list:

```go
list := tela.UseElementRef()
return Div(Class("relative"),
    Div(Ref(list), Class("h-96 overflow-y-auto scroll-smooth"), rows),
    Button(OnClick(func(tela.MouseEvent) { list.ScrollTo(0, 0) }), Text("Top")))
```

`ElementRef` is an alias of `core.ElementRef`, declared in an internal package of the module. pkg.go.dev shows only the alias; the exported fields and methods of the aliased type, listed here, are part of the API:

```go
type ElementRef struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

#### func UseElementRef

```go
func UseElementRef() ElementRef
```

UseElementRef returns the [`ElementRef`](#type-elementref) of this hook slot, the same on every build. Attach it to an element with h.Ref, then act on the element from handlers and effects (React's useRef with a DOM element):

```go
func Search() tela.Node {
    input := tela.UseElementRef()
    tela.UseMount(func() func() {
        input.Focus()
        return nil
    })
    return Div(Ref(input), TabIndex(0), Class("rounded-md p-2 focus:ring-2"), Text("Search"))
}
```

#### func (ElementRef) Blur

```go
func (r ElementRef) Blur()
```

Blur removes the focus from the element if it has it (HTML's blur()): nothing is focused afterwards.

#### func (ElementRef) Bounds

```go
func (r ElementRef) Bounds() Rect
```

Bounds returns the border box of the element in window coordinates and logical pixels, as it was last laid out and painted: moved by the scroll offsets of the containers around it and by its own transform and those of its ancestors, as the axis-aligned bounding box of the transformed box (getBoundingClientRect). The window's top-left corner is (0, 0). An inline element (a Span in a paragraph) has the union of its fragments, and an element with display: contents that of its children. It is the zero Rect for an element that is not mounted, is display: none, or has not been laid out yet. Call it from event handlers and effects; UseBounds gives a Value that follows it.

#### func (ElementRef) Focus

```go
func (r ElementRef) Focus()
```

Focus focuses the element, if it is focusable (HTML's focus()): OnBlur runs on the element that loses the focus and OnFocus on this one.

#### func (ElementRef) Focused

```go
func (r ElementRef) Focused() bool
```

Focused reports whether the element is the focused element of its window (also while the window itself does not have keyboard focus).

#### func (ElementRef) ScrollBy

```go
func (r ElementRef) ScrollBy(dx, dy float32)
```

ScrollBy scrolls the element by (dx, dy) from its current offsets (see ScrollTo).

#### func (ElementRef) ScrollIntoView

```go
func (r ElementRef) ScrollIntoView()
```

ScrollIntoView scrolls every scroll container around the element so that it is visible, moving each as little as possible (CSSOM View's scrollIntoView with block and inline "nearest"); each container jumps or animates as its scroll-behavior says. It does nothing when the element is not mounted or not displayed.

#### func (ElementRef) ScrollOffset

```go
func (r ElementRef) ScrollOffset() (x, y float32)
```

ScrollOffset returns the element's scroll offsets (the DOM's scrollLeft and scrollTop): zero when it is not a scroll container or not mounted. During a smooth scroll it is the current, animated position.

#### func (ElementRef) ScrollTo

```go
func (r ElementRef) ScrollTo(x, y float32)
```

ScrollTo scrolls the element to offsets (x, y), clamped to its extents (CSSOM View's scrollTo): at once, or animated when it has scroll-smooth. It does nothing for an element that is not a scroll container (overflow auto, scroll or hidden) or not mounted.

#### func (ElementRef) ScrollToIndex

```go
func (r ElementRef) ScrollToIndex(i int, align ScrollAlign)
```

ScrollToIndex scrolls a VirtualList so that item i is in view, placed as align says (TanStack Virtual's scrollToIndex; see the comment at the top of virtual.go): at once, or animated when the list has scroll-smooth, like ScrollTo. i is clamped to the items. It does nothing when the element is not a mounted VirtualList, has no items or does not scroll (overflow-visible).

#### func (ElementRef) Select

```go
func (r ElementRef) Select()
```

Select selects the whole value of the text field the ref is attached to (HTML's select()) and fires OnSelect; it does nothing on other elements.

#### func (ElementRef) SelectionRange

```go
func (r ElementRef) SelectionRange() (start, end int)
```

SelectionRange returns the selection of the text field the ref is attached to in UTF-8 byte offsets of its value, ordered (HTML's selectionStart and selectionEnd); 0, 0 for other elements.

#### func (ElementRef) SetSelectionRange

```go
func (r ElementRef) SetSelectionRange(start, end int)
```

SetSelectionRange selects the bytes \[start, end) of the value of the text field the ref is attached to (UTF-8 byte offsets, clamped to the value and moved to grapheme cluster boundaries; start \> end selects nothing at end), as HTML's setSelectionRange, and fires OnSelect when it changed. It does nothing on other elements.

#### func (ElementRef) Value

```go
func (r ElementRef) Value() string
```

Value returns the value of the text field the ref is attached to (with the text an IME is composing, as the DOM's input.value), "" for other elements: mainly for uncontrolled fields.

Key is a logical key: what the key means with the active layout and modifiers (a W3C KeyboardEvent key value). It is a named key, one of the Key constants ("Enter", "Escape", "ArrowLeft", "Shift"), or the character the key types ("a", "A", "é", " " for the space bar).
